coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 1.5-2x (hip region at 3-4x) with a grid labelled in scan pixels and raised contrast. Joint points are estimated joint centres, not skin landmarks: shoulder = centre of the humeral head under the deltoid; hip = greater trochanter, taken about 25-35 px in from the rear contour of the buttock at the level of the thigh's midline (the least certain point, about +-10 px); knee = centre of the knee between its front and back contours; ankle = centre of the malleolus; toe = tip of the foot; heel = back of the heel; head = top of the skull (crown). Every point set was drawn back onto its crop (dots + segments) and corrected until it sat on the joint; only points that passed are kept. Angles are computed by atan2 from these points; with a +-10 px hip, segment angles carry about +-5 deg. Heights are 'ground y minus point y' in scan pixels, with each frame's own ground (the sole line of the planted feet), because every frame comes from a different camera and the floor line differs by a few pixels between frames. The man faces RIGHT (forward = +x). Only the near leg is measured: the far leg is hidden behind it except for the far toes. 'hipRiseFromSeatedPx' is relative to 185 px, the mean seated hip height of frames 1-6. A standing hip height cannot be measured on this plate (he never stands laterally: by frames 9-10 he has turned and walks away from the camera), so lengths are not normalised to L; see findings for the conversion via plate 236.

findings: Numbering checked on the full scan: the lateral row is the BOTTOM row, numbered 1-10 left to right; the man faces right. He rises and, from frame 7 on, turns away from the camera and walks off, so frames 9-10 are rear-oblique and he is moving away from the lens.

Timing: the whole plate is 0.83 s. Forward lean starts at frame 3 (0.18 s); the hips stay on the seat (hip height 177-191 px, constant within error) until frame 6-7; seat-off falls between frames 7 and 8 (0.55-0.64 s), at the moment of largest trunk lean; by frame 10 (0.83 s) he is nearly upright and stepping. The lean-forward preparation takes about 0.4 s, the lift to near-upright about 0.2-0.3 s.

Trunk lean (hip-shoulder line from vertical, + forward): -8.5 (leaning back on the chair) at frame 1, then 2, 7, 15, 22 and 34 deg at frames 3-7. Hip (trunk-thigh) interior angle closes from 106 to 73 deg. The peak lean coincides with seat-off.

Knees: about 90 deg interior (89-95) from frame 1 to frame 8: the knee does not extend until the hips leave the seat. Meanwhile the shank tilts forward from 6 to 18 deg (the knee travels forward over the planted foot) and the hip slides forward so the ankle is 152 px ahead of the hip at frame 1 and 90 px at frame 8: the feet are effectively drawn back under the body before the lift.

Feet stay planted and flat through frames 1-8 (toe and heel on the ground line in every frame). Seated thigh 8 deg below horizontal (knee slightly lower than the hip), rising to about 17-24 deg below horizontal at seat-off as the hips go up.

Comparison with figures/human.json motions.sit (looping seated idle on an edge, 2.0 s, lower 19, legsForward 20, legsUp 23, kick 2): our sit has no rise, so this plate is the reference for a separate one-shot 'stand up'. Our seated knee (about 81 deg interior) is close to the plate's 89-92 deg; our thigh points 15 deg ABOVE horizontal (legsUp) where the plate's is 8 deg below; our trunk keeps its 6 deg rest lean where the plate's sitter leans back 5-9 deg against the chair. Our feet hang 4 units above the foot line and swing; the plate's are planted flat.

A one-shot 'stand up' transition, from this plate: about 0.8 s in total (8 frames at 10 fps, or 6 at 8 fps). Phase 1 (about half the time): hips stay put, trunk pitches forward from upright to about 30-35 deg, knees stay at about 90 deg while the shins tilt forward about 12 deg (knees over toes), arms reach forward. Phase 2 (seat-off at the peak lean): hips rise and the trunk straightens together, knees extend; most of the height is gained in the last 2-3 frames. Feet planted throughout; the turn and step away in frames 9-10 are this sitter's exit, not part of the rise.

Not measured: the far leg (hidden); shoulder in frames 8-10 and leg joints in frames 9-10 (body turned, rear-oblique view); a normalised standing hip height (he never stands laterally; at frame 10 he is farther from the lens, so his 295 px hip height understates it); seat height; hand positions. Scale differs from plate 236 (seated shank here 133-151 px vs 106-111 px), so pixel values must not be mixed between the two plates; use ratios and angles.
